label: 0024 · Starter extended back to 1997 on a fixed 747-site network: 2003 Tokachi-oki windows, Boso slow slip events and 2000–2002 volcanic steps removed, UNR positions (exploratory MCMC)
description: The Boso pilot (0021 with the Boso slow slip events removed) extended back to April 1997 on a fixed station network: the 747 GEONET sites with data in every year from 1997-04-01 to 2025-05-09, plus 112 far-field stations, so the station set doesn't change through the record. Every window was rebuilt and rerun. Before 2005 there are three windows of about 790 days (April 1997 to September 2003), then windows of 30, 91, 182 and 365 days after the 2003 Tokachi-oki Mw 8.3, with free reverse dip-slip on the Japan Trench for the first 91 days as after Tohoku, and a postseismic window up to the 2005 Miyagi-oki earthquake. Also removed as steps: a 2002 Boso slow slip event found by the matched filter, the 2000 Usu eruption, the 2000 Miyake-jima dike intrusion and the 2002 Hachijo-jima dike intrusion. From August 2005 the windows are the pilot's and match it (fit ratio 0.98 on the pilot's stations; Tohoku afterslip Mw 8.35–8.44 against 8.36–8.45). The early windows show coupling changes: Tokai drops from 0.67 to 0.14 during the 2000–2005 slow slip and recovers to 0.5–0.6; off Sanriku coupling rises from 0.53 to 0.68; off Hokkaido it is 0.97–0.99 before Tokachi-oki. Tokachi-oki trench afterslip reaches Mw 7.48 at 30 days and 7.64 at 1 yr; the first 30-day window still misfits Kushiro and Nemuro. Noise is higher before 2003 (fit 4.1–4.5 mm/yr against 3.2–3.6 after).
